title: Iterated halving on a countable ball cover gives a full-measure Borel countably m-rectifiable set (Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 ⇐, final iteration)
statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, E := ℝ^{m+1}, D ⊆ E open, and μ a Borel measure on E with μ(E \ D) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ D. Assume (★): for every open U ⊆ E whose closure Ū is compact and contained in D there is a closed countably m-rectifiable set Γ ⊆ E with μ(U \ Γ) ≤ μ(U)/2. Then there is a Borel countably m-rectifiable set R ⊆ E with μ(E \ R) = 0.
lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (D : Set (Euclid (m + 1))) (μ : Measure (Euclid (m + 1))), IsOpen D → μ Dᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Euclid (m + 1)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ D → μ K ≠ ∞) → (∀ U : Set (Euclid (m + 1)), IsOpen U → IsCompact (closure U) → closure U ⊆ D → ∃ Γ : Set (Euclid (m + 1)), IsClosed Γ ∧ CountablyRectifiable m Γ ∧ μ (U \ Γ) ≤ μ U / 2) → ∃ R : Set (Euclid (m + 1)), MeasurableSet R ∧ CountablyRectifiable m R ∧ μ Rᶜ = 0
